workshop_label: ESSENTIAL PROCESS REVIEW | DRAFT FOR REVIEW
title: SIA Incident Management
subtitle: Two-day online Essential demonstration and process fit workshop
purpose: Introduce Essential and assess how closely its current incident processes meet SIA needs, in priority order: Injury/Illness, Environmental Incident, Property Damage, Notice of Violation, and Near Miss. Agree where the standard process can be adopted, identify minor workflow and field changes, and capture OHM/Resolver API and reporting requirements.
daily_format: Session 1: 9:30 a.m.-1:30 p.m. EST (4 hours total; 3 hours 30 minutes working time). Session 2: 9:30 a.m.-1:00 p.m. EST (3 hours 30 minutes total; 3 hours working time). Each session includes two 15-minute breaks. Agenda tables use the 24-hour clock; all times are EST. Dates and the online platform are to be confirmed. No lunch is scheduled within these half-day windows. Use a live Essential demonstration, screen sharing, and a shared fit/gap and decision log.
scope: Review all five incident types in the stated priority order. For each, compare intake, investigation, follow-up, and closure with SIA practice. Include client-configured OHM and Resolver APIs, minor form/workflow/field changes, hours worked, and overall incident reporting. Capture larger changes separately for impact review.

days.summary: Introduce Essential; compare Injury/Illness and Environmental Incident with SIA processes. Define OHM and Resolver feed requirements and minor changes.

rows.outcome: Confirm workshop outputs, SIA decision owners, and the five-topic priority order. Agree how process matches, gaps, decisions, and actions will be recorded.
Review navigation, incident records, role-based tasks, investigation, follow-up, and closure. Confirm the Essential baseline being demonstrated and the comparison approach for SIA.

Walk through the current Essential process using an SIA scenario. Compare first report, investigation, follow-up, and closure; confirm matches and identify minor workflow and field changes, including fields needed for OHM data.

Define requirements for the client-configured API sending OHM incident records to Intelex. Confirm first-report-of-injury creation and investigation/follow-up triggers; review field mapping, source identifiers, duplicate prevention, error handling, and access. Agree minor changes and owners.

Walk through the current Essential environmental process using an SIA scenario. Compare first report, investigation, follow-up, and closure; confirm matches and identify minor workflow and field changes needed for SIA and the Resolver feed.

Define requirements for the client-configured API sending Resolver environmental incident records to Intelex. Confirm first-report creation and investigation/follow-up triggers; review field mapping, source identifiers, duplicate prevention, error handling, and ownership of minor changes.
Confirm process matches, gaps, and agreed changes. Review open questions, actions, owners, and dependencies; assign any OHM/Resolver mapping follow-up and preparation needed for Day 2.

rows.outcome: Confirm Day 1 outcomes and open dependencies. Agree decisions needed today and preserve the remaining topic priority order.

rows.session: 4. Notice of Violation: Essential vs SIA
rows.outcome: Walk through the current Essential process and compare SIA notice capture, ownership, response deadlines, investigation, follow-up, and closure evidence. Agree process matches and required minor field/workflow changes.
Walk through the current Essential process and compare SIA reporting, classification, investigation, follow-up, and closure. Confirm required roles, process matches, and minor field/workflow changes.

Define the hours-worked source, data owner, reporting frequency, reporting period, and location/worker coverage. Agree entry or import needs, validation and correction rules, and alignment with incident measures where hours are used.

Review Essential reporting against SIA needs across all five incident types. Confirm priority measures, definitions, filters, trends, open/overdue follow-up views, audiences, and exports; identify gaps and owners for sample reports.

Agree the consolidated fit/gap record, minor change list, API/reporting follow-ups, and unresolved decisions. Confirm actions, owners, target dates, dependencies, and the next review of the workshop outputs.

closeout.expected_outputs: A fit/gap comparison for each of the five incident types, in priority order; agreed adoption of Essential steps; a prioritized minor workflow/field change list; OHM and Resolver API requirements, mapping actions, and first-report/workflow triggers; hours-worked and overall incident reporting requirements; a decision/action log with owners, target dates, and dependencies. Mark each requirement as confirmed, provisional, or unresolved.
closeout.participants: Core: SIA incident process owner, safety/EHS representatives, operational investigators or supervisors, Essential demonstrator/Intelex solution lead, facilitator, and scribe. Day 1 targeted: clinic/OHM owner, environmental/Resolver owner, client API/integration team, and data/access representatives. Day 2 targeted: Property Damage, Notice of Violation, and Near Miss process owners; hours-worked data owner; reporting lead. Ensure decision makers attend their sessions or nominate delegates.
closeout.preparation: Prepare the current Essential demonstration environment and one anonymized SIA scenario for each incident type. Share current SIA forms, workflows, roles, and follow-up/closure requirements. Bring OHM and Resolver sample payloads or field lists, source identifiers, API constraints, and integration owners. Provide hours-worked source examples, reporting periods, sample incident reports, and desired measures. Confirm dates, platform, participant availability for the stated EST times, and shared fit/gap log; test online access and screen sharing.
closeout.scope_control: Use the updated SIA brief as the workshop baseline: client-configured APIs send OHM Injury/Illness and Resolver Environmental Incident records to Intelex, which creates first reports and starts investigation/follow-up workflows. Focus on Essential adoption and minor form/workflow/field changes; record larger changes for impact review. Reconcile the earlier proposed ADR-064 with this OHM/API direction when documenting outcomes. Address ADR-091 incident-to-NCR/CAR linkage only where a demonstrated process requires it; record unresolved linkage questions without expanding this workshop into a separate application redesign.
